newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD could postpone tax talks in protest.
newsitem.headline: German SPD could postpone tax talks in protest.

text.p: Germany's main opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Friday they would not rule out postponing key talks with the government over tax reform in protest at Bonn's plans to slash aid to coal miners.

The government proposed late on Thursday to cut aid to the coal industry to 3.8 billion marks in the year 2005 from around 10 billion marks annually now. Government and opposition are scheduled to meet on Saturday to discuss tax reform.
A spokesman for the SPD parliamentary faction said the party was considering a postponement of the talks.
Heinz Schleusser, finance minister of North Rhine-Westphalia and a participant in the tax talks, said earlier he would boycott Saturday's round in protest against the government coal proposal.

A spokesman for the Federal Finance Ministry said the SPD had not yet notified it of any change in the scheduled Saturday talks. He said he had learned from newspapers of Schleusser's intention not to attend.

The tax reform talks, two inconclusive rounds of which were held last week, are aimed at reaching a cross-party agreement on a package that would cut rates and simplify the tax system to stimulate investment and create jobs.
